key_insight: LACUNA introduces a testbed for checking whether LLM unlearning actually removes knowledge from the model, not just from its outputs. It focuses on evaluating how precisely methods can localize and erase the targeted information inside the network.
problem_solved: Current unlearning benchmarks mostly measure output behavior, which can miss whether sensitive information still remains encoded in model parameters. This paper addresses the gap in evaluating the true localization precision of post hoc unlearning methods.
method: Builds a benchmark/testbed specifically for localization-precision evaluation in LLM unlearning.
Assesses localize-first, unlearn-second methods by probing whether targeted knowledge is removed from the intended model components.
Moves evaluation beyond output-level checks to internal model-level verification of forgetting.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, LACUNA helps determine whether unlearning methods genuinely reduce privacy and memorization risks. It provides a more reliable way to compare methods and avoid false confidence from output-only evaluations.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing: trained LLM -> sensitive data memorization -> localization -> unlearning -> evaluation.
Side-by-side comparison chart of output-level vs model-level unlearning evaluation.
Heatmap of model parameters highlighting localized vs lingering knowledge.
Icon set for privacy, memory, forgetting, and verification.
paper_title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
paper_authors: Matteo Boglioni, Thibault Rousset, Siva Reddy, Marius Mosbach, Verna Dankers
